- Model consistently underestimates prices during sharp upward spikes (e.g., 44+ → 45+ → 46+), especially in 2024 Q2.
- Model overestimates prices in early 2024 (e.g., 38+ forecast vs 41+ true) when historical mean is low.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: forecasts too low after high recent prices, and too high after low recent prices.
- Model lags in capturing sudden downward shocks (e.g., 45.93 → 34.33) — underreacts to sharp drops.
- Overshoots after spikes: forecasts peak too early or too high after a price surge, then drops below true.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonality or policy-driven volatility (e.g., EU ETS auction cycles) — over-smooths transitions.
- Forecasts are too conservative in high-variance periods — underestimates risk premium or supply-demand shocks.
- Model exhibits “memory decay” — recent high prices are not sufficiently weighted in forecasts, leading to underestimation of continuation.
